# Kyoto Solo Trip Plan: 4 Low-Stress Days

A calm, walk-friendly Kyoto route for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13** with temples, local snacks, and minimal backtracking.
Budget is kept under **JPY 45,000 total excluding flights**, using mostly public transit, short walks, and low-cost admissions.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary
### Day 1: Higashiyama Temple Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Must-see 1:** Kiyomizu-dera
- **Must-see 2:** Yasaka Pagoda area / Sannenzaka–Ninenzaka stroll
- **Food stop:** Gion snack break for yatsuhashi or matcha soft serve
- **Transit time:** Kyoto Station → Kiyomizu-dera area: **20–25 min**
- **Pace:** Start early, stay mostly on foot, and keep the afternoon flexible for cafés or rest

### Day 2: Arashiyama and Riverside Temples
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Must-see 1:** Tenryu-ji
- **Must-see 2:** Bamboo Grove and Togetsukyo Bridge area
- **Food stop:** Arashiyama tofu lunch or a simple soba set
- **Transit time:** Central Kyoto → Arashiyama: **25–35 min**
- **Pace:** Best as a slow half-day with scenic walking and one temple cluster

### Day 3: Northern Kyoto Cultural Circuit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Must-see 1:** Kinkaku-ji
- **Must-see 2:** Ryoan-ji
- **Food stop:** Local rice bowl or a small tea-and-sweets stop near the temple route
- **Transit time:** Arashiyama/central Kyoto → Kinkaku-ji area: **30–45 min**
- **Pace:** Go temple-to-temple by bus/taxi only if needed; otherwise keep the day simple and unhurried

### Day 4: Fushimi Inari + Easy Final Stroll
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- **Must-see 1:** Fushimi Inari Taisha
- **Must-see 2:** Tofuku-ji area or a relaxed final walk through Gion/Philosopher’s Path if energy is low
- **Food stop:** Inari-area aburaage, onigiri, or a station snack set
- **Transit time:** Kyoto Station → Fushimi Inari: **5–10 min**
- **Pace:** Start early, hike only as far as feels good, and leave room for a slow final afternoon

## Budget Cap Plan: JPY 45,000
| Category | Estimated Cost |
|---|---:|
| Temple admissions and small entry fees | JPY 4,000 |
| Local transit (bus/subway/train) | JPY 3,500 |
| Food and snacks | JPY 16,000 |
| Coffee/tea breaks | JPY 3,000 |
| Rainy-day backup entry | JPY 2,000 |
| Buffer for extras | JPY 16,500 |
| **Total** | **JPY 45,000** |

### Cost Control Notes
- Keep lunches in the **JPY 900–1,500** range.
- Use walking between nearby sights whenever possible.
- Choose **one paid indoor backup** instead of adding extra attractions.
- Buy snacks from stations or temple streets rather than full dessert cafés every day.

## Rainy-Day Backup Options
- **Kyoto National Museum**: good indoor cultural backup if weather is poor.
- **Nishiki Market**: easy covered food stop for local snacks, pickles, tofu, and sweets.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Nishiki Market**: easy covered food stop for local snacks, pickles, tofu, and sweets, Kyoto, Japan
- **Kyoto Railway Museum**: only if you want a full indoor day with very low walking.

## Quick Actions

## Sources
- Kyoto City tourism: https://kyoto.travel/en
- Kyoto National Museum: https://www.kyohaku.go.jp/eng/
- Google Maps route planning: https://www.google.com/maps
